stem: What population was followed in this tumour-informed ctDNA study?
choices: Eight children with solid tumours, sampled longitudinally
Eight adults with solid tumours, sampled longitudinally
Eighty children with solid tumours, sampled once
Eight children with haematological malignancies, sampled longitudinally
answer: Eight children with solid tumours, sampled longitudinally
label: Results · cohort

stem: How many tumour-specific mutations did each personalized SiMSen-Seq panel target?
choices: Between 4 and 10
Exactly 10 in every patient
Between 20 and 50
Between 1 and 3
answer: Between 4 and 10
label: Results · panel design

stem: By how much did UMIs reduce the background error rate, and between which values?
choices: About 55-fold, from 0.366% to 0.007%
About 55-fold, from 0.007% to 0.366%
About 5-fold, from 0.366% to 0.07%
About 550-fold, from 0.366% to 0.0007%
answer: About 55-fold, from 0.366% to 0.007%
label: Results · error correction

stem: What happened to the average background error rate as the UMI family size cutoff rose from 2 to 30?
choices: It did not change significantly, staying between 0.004% and 0.006%
It fell steadily, reaching about 0.001% at a cutoff of 30
It rose steadily, passing 0.02% at a cutoff of 30
It fell sharply up to a cutoff of 10 and then plateaued
answer: It did not change significantly, staying between 0.004% and 0.006%
label: Results · error correction

stem: Which substitution type dominated the raw sequencing errors before UMI correction?
choices: Transversions, at 92.2%
Transitions, at 92.2%
Deletions, at 92.2%
Insertions, at 92.2%
answer: Transversions, at 92.2%
label: Results · error types

stem: What did UMI correction do to the balance between transversions and transitions?
choices: Narrowed it to 58.6% versus 41.4%
Widened it to 98% versus 2%
Left it unchanged at 92.2% versus 7.8%
Reversed it to 7.8% versus 92.2%
answer: Narrowed it to 58.6% versus 41.4%
label: Results · error types

stem: Among the 66 assays, how many had an average error rate above 0.01% at a family size of 2?
choices: Five, of which two exceeded 0.02%
Twenty, of which five exceeded 0.02%
Thirty-three, of which two exceeded 0.02%
None exceeded 0.01%
answer: Five, of which two exceeded 0.02%
label: Results · per-assay error

stem: What explained the raised error rates of 0.03% to 0.08% in four of Patient 7's samples?
choices: One assay performed poorly and returned few detected molecules
The samples were sequenced at a lower UMI family size cutoff
The cell-free DNA input for those samples was unusually high
The samples were drawn after chemotherapy had begun
answer: One assay performed poorly and returned few detected molecules
label: Results · outlier samples

stem: In the three-way analysis of variance, which factors significantly affected the error rate?
choices: Assay and sample, but not the UMI family size cutoff
The UMI family size cutoff, but not assay or sample
All three factors significantly
None of the three factors significantly
answer: Assay and sample, but not the UMI family size cutoff
label: Results · variance analysis

stem: How did background errors in genomic DNA from blood cells compare with those in cell-free DNA?
choices: Significantly lower, being intact molecules spared the same degradation
Significantly higher, because far more DNA mass is loaded
Indistinguishable from cell-free DNA across the whole range
Lower, but only at UMI family size cutoffs above 10
answer: Significantly lower, being intact molecules spared the same degradation
label: Results · control material

stem: In the mutation-positive PCDHGA4 example, how far did UMI correction cut the background error?
label: Results · worked example

stem: What happened to the mutant allele frequency when UMI correction was applied to that sample?
choices: Essentially unchanged, 0.299% of raw against 0.300% of consensus reads
Roughly halved, 0.299% of raw against 0.150% of consensus reads
Roughly doubled, 0.299% of raw against 0.600% of consensus reads
Lost entirely, falling below the assay's detection limit
answer: Essentially unchanged, 0.299% of raw against 0.300% of consensus reads
label: Results · worked example

stem: In the mutation-negative CHD5 sample, what became of the 4 mutated reads seen among 339,374 raw reads?
choices: None survived UMI correction; they were false positives
All 4 were confirmed as genuine ctDNA molecules
2 of the 4 survived as consensus reads
They increased to 26 consensus reads after correction
answer: None survived UMI correction; they were false positives
label: Results · worked example

stem: What independently supported the negative CHD5 call?
choices: The patient stayed disease-free through five years of follow-up
A confirmatory digital PCR assay on the same sample
A repeat plasma draw one week later
Whole-exome sequencing of a later relapse specimen
answer: The patient stayed disease-free through five years of follow-up
label: Results · worked example

stem: On average, how many UMIs does one double-stranded DNA molecule generate in SiMSen-Seq?
label: Results · molecule counting

stem: What share of input DNA molecules was detected at a UMI family size of at least 2, against at least 30?
choices: 19.1% against 9.1%
9.1% against 19.1%
19.1% against 17.5%
55% against 19.1%
answer: 19.1% against 9.1%
label: Results · molecule counting

stem: What did the linear correlation identify as a major driver of intersample variation in detected molecules?
choices: The amount of cell-free DNA input
The UMI family size cutoff applied
The patient's tumour type
The number of assays in the panel
answer: The amount of cell-free DNA input
label: Results · molecule counting

stem: How wide was the gap between the best and worst performing assay within a patient's panel?
choices: From 1.4-fold in one patient to 19-fold in another
From 1.4-fold to 2.2-fold across patients
From 19-fold to 55-fold across patients
Under 1.5-fold in every patient
answer: From 1.4-fold in one patient to 19-fold in another
label: Results · assay variation

stem: What was the range of average detected molecules per sample and time point?
label: Results · molecule counting

stem: Which UMI family size cutoff did the study conclude was optimal?
choices: At least 2
At least 5
At least 10
At least 30
answer: At least 2
label: Results · conclusion

stem: How was a sample defined as ctDNA positive?
choices: At least one mutation called with a Q-score of 10 or more
At least two mutations called with a Q-score of 10 or more
At least one mutation at a variant allele frequency of 0.1% or more
At least half the panel's assays positive
answer: At least one mutation called with a Q-score of 10 or more
label: Results · calling rule

stem: What did baseline sampling show in the patients who had a day-0 sample?
choices: All five were ctDNA positive, spanning 1.05 to 3855 molecules per mL
Three of five were ctDNA positive, spanning 1.05 to 3855 molecules per mL
All five were ctDNA positive, spanning 55.5 to 8070 molecules per mL
All eight were ctDNA positive, spanning 1.05 to 3855 molecules per mL
answer: All five were ctDNA positive, spanning 1.05 to 3855 molecules per mL
label: Results · clinical monitoring

stem: What was Patient 1's peak ctDNA level, and what followed treatment?
choices: 55.5 molecules per mL, then negative samples and complete regression
55.5 molecules per mL, then persistently positive samples
3855 molecules per mL, then negative samples and complete regression
11.0 molecules per mL, then residual disease at surgery
answer: 55.5 molecules per mL, then negative samples and complete regression
label: Results · clinical monitoring

stem: What did Patient 2's sample taken one day before planned surgery show?
choices: Residual disease at 11.0 mutated molecules per mL
No detectable ctDNA, as in the preceding samples
A rise to 55.5 mutated molecules per mL
Residual disease at 1.05 mutated molecules per mL
answer: Residual disease at 11.0 mutated molecules per mL
label: Results · clinical monitoring

stem: Which patients relapsed, and when relative to their last blood sample?
choices: Patients 2 and 5, 6 to 7 months afterwards
Patients 1 and 7, 6 to 7 months afterwards
Patients 2 and 5, within 1 month afterwards
Patients 2 and 5, 3 to 4 years afterwards
answer: Patients 2 and 5, 6 to 7 months afterwards
label: Results · outcomes

stem: What happened to the number of detected mutations at higher UMI family size cutoffs?
choices: It stayed the same or fell
It rose, as noise was removed
It rose up to a cutoff of 10, then fell
It became too variable to compare
answer: It stayed the same or fell
label: Results · cutoff effects

stem: What share of the cell-free DNA molecules estimated by fluorometric quantification was actually detected?
choices: About 19%
About 50%
About 90%
About 2%
answer: About 19%
label: Discussion · recovery

stem: What may cause fluorometric quantification to overestimate cell-free DNA concentration?
choices: Carrier RNA used during extraction
Fragmentation of the cell-free DNA
Inhibitors carried over from plasma
Loss of DNA at the concentration step
answer: Carrier RNA used during extraction
label: Discussion · recovery

stem: How many reads per sample does a 10-assay panel on 10 ng of DNA require?
choices: At least about 137,000, rising linearly with the cutoff
At least about 13,700, rising linearly with the cutoff
At least about 1.4 million, rising linearly with the cutoff
At least about 137,000, independent of the cutoff
answer: At least about 137,000, rising linearly with the cutoff
label: Discussion · sequencing cost

stem: What does the paper propose to counter sampling ambiguity at low variant allele frequencies?
choices: Targeting several mutations per patient
Raising the UMI family size cutoff
Increasing sequencing depth per UMI
Drawing plasma at shorter intervals
answer: Targeting several mutations per patient
label: Discussion · sensitivity

stem: Which UMI parameters did the authors state they had not assessed?
choices: Edit distance, UMI length and UMI structure
Family size and edit distance
Sequencing depth and read length
Barcoding PCR cycle number and primer concentration
answer: Edit distance, UMI length and UMI structure
label: Limitations
